c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: Your micro:bit is plugged into the Cutebot. Which one is the brain that holds your program?
c1.why: The micro:bit holds the program. The Cutebot is the body that carries out what the program says.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: You download a program, unplug the cable, then switch the car on. Your face appears. Why?

A.text: The program is stored inside the micro:bit

B.text: The face is painted on the screen

C.text: The cable is still sending the program

D.text: The computer is remembering it for you

c2.why: Downloading copies the program into the micro:bit. The cable only carries it across once.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: A pair switch their car on and nothing happens at all. What should they check first?

D.text: The floor they are driving on

c3.why: Weak or missing batteries look exactly like a bug in the code. Power comes first, always.

r1.label: Q1

A.text: Every time you press a button

B.text: Once, the moment the program starts

D.text: Only when the car is on the floor

r1.why: Blocks at the top level sit inside `on start`, and `on start` runs once at the beginning.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: What do you see on the micro:bit screen?

A.text: The happy face for about half a second, then the sad face, which stays

B.text: Both faces at the same time

C.text: Nothing, because two icon blocks cancel out

D.text: A happy face, then a sad face a second later

r2.why: `show icon` holds its picture for about 0.6 seconds by default, so you do see the happy face first. Then the next block replaces it — and the last icon block is the one that stays.

r3.label: Q3

A.text: A happy face, then a heart that stays

D.text: A heart for a moment, then a happy face that stays

r3.why: The blocks run top to bottom. The heart shows first, then the happy face replaces it and stays.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: The car sits on the floor with this program running. What do the wheels do?

A.text: They turn only while the face is showing

D.text: They do not turn at all

r4.why: Nothing in this program speaks to the motors, so the wheels never turn. A program that shows a face is not a program that drives.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: A student wanted a happy face and got a sad one. Which change fixes it?

A.text: Add another happy face block at the top

C.text: Change the happy face block to a heart

d1.why: The last icon block wins. Deleting the sad face leaves the happy one on the screen.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: A pair say their car is broken because it will not drive. Their program shows a face and nothing else. What is actually wrong?

A.text: The micro:bit is in the wrong way round

B.text: Nothing is broken — the program never tells the wheels to move

C.text: They downloaded it to the wrong car

D.text: The car is broken and needs a new motor

d2.why: The car does exactly what the program says. No motor block means no movement — that is not a fault.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Put these steps in the right order to get a program onto your car: 1 switch the car on · 2 write the blocks in MakeCode · 3 unplug the cable · 4 download to the micro:bit
b1.why: Write it, send it, unplug it, then switch the car on and put it down. Later programs make the wheels turn, so a car switched on while still on the cable can drive off the desk.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: Which part goes with which job? A = micro:bit, B = motor, C = sonar, D = battery box. Which pairing is right?
b2.why: The sonar — the two silver eyes at the front — measures distance. The micro:bit holds the program, the motors turn the wheels, and the batteries supply the power.
